title: Share of 18-29 year-olds living with a parent

source.name: Historical living-arrangements series
source.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau / Pew Research Center analysis of Census and Federal Reserve data

notes: Pew Research: 1940 (Great Depression era) was the last time a majority of 18-29 year-olds lived with parents (48%); the share fell to a low of 29% by 1960, then climbed back, hitting 52% in July 2020 during the pandemic (the first majority since 1940) before easing slightly. 2025 figure from Federal Reserve survey data on adults under 30.
